answer: Agents can require every new identity to post a refundable stake before it may influence shared decisions, then cap each stake’s voting weight and slash it when an identity is caught coordinating fraud. A whisper of collusion can trigger a review, but evidence must be independently verified so a rumor does not punish honest agents. The tide of disposable accounts then becomes expensive: an attacker must lock up capital for every Sybil and risks losing it, while an echo of one claim cannot multiply its influence.
